title: Learner-gain survey instrument + outcome dashboard
context: open-coding-curriculum is an open CC-BY (prose) / MIT (code) curriculum of beginner programming lessons with graded, runnable exercises across languages. Every exercise carries a reference solution proven correct in CI (solutionVerified:true), learner code runs zero-install in-browser via WASM, and all content is machine-readable structured data so third parties can build on it. The project targets absolute beginners — self-learners, public-library patrons, under-resourced school students, career-changers — and operates under a donated-compute lane with no server-side execution of learner code and no partner confirmed yet (verifiedNeed:false). The project's primary success metric — 'at least 75% of surveyed learners agree they can do something they could not before' — depends on a survey instrument that does not yet exist. Without it, the learning-gain metric cannot be reported. The survey must be designed to collect ≥ 25 responses over a rolling 90-day post-adoption window.
objective: Design a learner-gain survey instrument for use by adopting partners, targeting ≥ 25 respondents over a rolling 90-day post-adoption window, with questions that measure whether learners can now do things they could not before; and specify an outcome dashboard for tracking aggregate results.
acceptanceCriteria: Survey instrument is designed with questions targeting the learning-gain metric: 'I can now write a program that does X, which I could not do before' (Likert-scale + open-ended follow-up).
Survey is designed to be administered by the education partner post-adoption (not the project team) to minimize Hawthorne effect.
Survey design targets ≥ 25 respondents over a rolling 90-day window; sampling strategy (e.g. end-of-session, post-module completion) is specified.
Target response rate (≥ 30%) and minimum sample size are documented with rationale.
An outcome dashboard specification is produced: what metrics are tracked, how they are aggregated, and how the 75%-agree threshold is calculated.
Survey instrument is reviewed for clarity and bias by at least one person with a background in education or evaluation methodology.
Privacy: no personally identifiable learner data is collected; survey is anonymous or pseudonymous.
output: A committed survey instrument (question bank, administration guide, privacy notes) and an outcome dashboard specification document.
